profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 43 (Digital Realty missing-address campaign): added a multi-source agreed address.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, Digital Realty New Jersey EWR10, matches multiple independently agreeing aggregators, UPSTACK, Inflect, DataCenterMap, and Macraes Blue Book, all giving 300 Boulevard East, Weehawken, NJ 07086, sometimes written 300 JFK Boulevard East.

profile.facility_type_note: Part of Digital Realty's New York/New Jersey metro campus, spanning Clifton, Piscataway Township, and Weehawken, NJ (EWR airport code used in Digital Realty's naming). Confirmed addresses per Digital Realty's own site include EWR21 at 2 Peekay Drive (Clifton) and EWR12 at 365 S. Randolphville Road (Piscataway).

reading.body:
This facility sits in Weehawken as part of Digital Realty's larger New York/New Jersey metro campus, which also includes mapped buildings in Clifton and Piscataway Township. The operator has not published the critical IT megawatts for this specific building, so its true scale relative to other facilities in the region cannot be calculated from available data.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities total, but only 5 publish power figures to operators' spec pages, accounting for 111.3 MW combined. This facility's rank cannot be determined because its megawatts are not confirmed from a tier-1 source.

Without published power, the site cannot yet serve as a reference point for assessing AI hosting density, grid demand, or buildout trajectory in the Newark metro. The operator should publish per-building IT load to enable comparative analysis across its portfolio.
